subject: End-of-service removal criteria & notification — redlines for MSA/order form
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: End-of-service removal criteria & notification — redlines for MSA/order form

Hi Karthik, Marissa,

Attaching our proposed redlines for the MSA and the ACME order form. The commercial team needs clarity on three linked items before we can move the updated order form through DocuSign:

- Term cadence and auto-renew trigger (we're proposing 12mo + 60d notice auto-renew opt-out)
- Offboarding / removal criteria (what counts as "service end" vs. migration support)
- Transitional support window and responsibilities for data export

Please review the attached MSA_Redline_v3.docx and OrderForm_ACME_Redline.pdf. High-level asks:
- Confirm whether we can accept mutual 60-day notice (we prefer mutual rather than unilateral 30/60 options)
- Replace "termination for convenience" with the limited mutual termination language in section 5.2 (see redline)
- Approve a 90-day standard transition support SOW rather than site-specific terms

Can you turn around guidance by EOD today? If legal needs to push any terms to the AE or Sales Ops, flag them and I'll coordinate the call.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MSA_Redline_v3.docx (docx), OrderForm_ACME_Redline.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: End-of-service removal criteria & notification — redlines for MSA/order form

Neha —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick notes from Legal after an initial pass (see attached Legal_CNTR_Notes.txt for line-by-line):

1) Auto-renew / notice window
- We can agree to a 12-month term with a mutual 60-day opt-out window. 
- Avoid unilateral shorter notice periods tied to specific product tiers; mutual notice reduces commercial escalations.

2) Termination for convenience
- Recommend keeping a mutual termination for convenience but limit it to non-performance scenarios with a 60-day cure period. Full unilateral "termination for convenience" with no cure or fee exposure is high risk.

3) Data export & transition
- We should commit to providing data export access for 60 days after termination (standard).
- If customer requests managed migration services, those should be scoped in a separate SOW and timeboxed (we can offer 90 days standard for paid transition support).

4) Early termination fee / pilot clauses
- If ACME is running a heavily discounted pilot, we should reserve the right to charge a prorated early termination fee. Please flag if this deal includes pilot discounts.

If the commercial team wants to push 90 days of guaranteed export instead of 60, we need to get explicit sponsor signoff and a change to pricing. Otherwise Legal will accept mutual 60-day export + 90-day paid SOW option.

I can join a quick 20-min call with ACME if they push back; otherwise, we can send the proposed language and track via DocuSign.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Legal_CNTR_Notes.txt

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed end-of-service language for MSA / order form — ACME (DocuSign link inside)

Tom —

Thanks again for the productive conversation earlier. Per our internal legal review, please find below the proposed language we've added to the MSA/Order Form focused on end-of-service and transition obligations. We tried to keep obligations mutual and operationally clear to avoid surprises at offboard time. If this looks good we can push the updated order form via DocuSign (link below).

Proposed snippet (high level):
"
1) Term and Renewal: The Initial Term shall be twelve (12) months. The Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term.

2) Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice; termination shall be mutual and subject to the cure and prorated fee provisions in Section 5.2.

3) Data Export & Transition: Following any termination or non-renewal, Redwood will permit Customer to export data for sixty (60) days at no additional charge. Managed migration services beyond sixty (60) days will be offered under a separate, time-limited SOW (standard offering: ninety (90) days at published professional services rates).
"

Next steps:
- If ACME accepts, click the DocuSign link and we will route for signatures.
- If ACME wants a longer managed transition window or changes to the termination fee, let us know and we will escalate to Legal for final signoff.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/ACME-OrderForm-2026

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Proposed_EndOfService_Snippet.txt

From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmecorp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-02-15T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed end-of-service language for MSA / order form — ACME (DocuSign link inside)

Neha, Karthik —

Appreciate the clear proposal. ACME is generally amenable to a mutual 60-day notice for non-renewal, but we have two asks before we can push to signature:

1) Data export window: 60 days is a little tight for our infrastructure team if there's significant data to move. We need 120 days of guaranteed export access at no additional charge (we will not require managed services by default).

2) Transition support: If managed migration is required, we prefer a 120-day window for paid migration services for enterprise migrations (we can agree to a capped rate but need the additional time).

3) Early termination fee: For deeply discounted pilots, we propose a clawback clause capped at 30% of remaining committed fees if ACME terminates within the first six months.

If these are dealbreakers, let's set up a 30-minute call tomorrow to align. I can make time at 10:30am PT.

Best,

Tom Liu
Head of Procurement | AcmeCorp
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachments: ACME_Counters_Annex.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed end-of-service language for MSA / order form — ACME (DocuSign link inside)

Tom —

Thanks for the quick response and clear asks. Short answers while I loop Legal: 

- Mutual 60-day notice: agreed on our side.
- Data export window: Legal prefers standard 60 days but is open to 90 days on commercial uplift. We cannot commit to 120 days at no charge without a pricing change or exec approval.
- Managed migration: we can offer a 90-day paid SOW as standard; we can discuss a one-time 120-day option if ACME is open to a modest professional services uplift.
- Early termination fee on pilots: reasonable ask; please confirm whether ACME considers the pilot a deeply discounted arrangement and provide the discount details so we can model a prorated clawback.

Next step: Karthik, can you confirm if Legal will accept the following fallback so we can avoid a CFO-level escalation?

Fallback proposal for ACME: mutual 60-day notice; 90-day no-charge export + 90-day paid managed migration SOW; early termination clawback capped at 30% for pilot discounts >50%.

Tom — if that works, I will update the DocuSign packet and route for signatures. If not, let's take the 30-min call at 10:30am PT as you suggested.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
